seoTitle: Jungian Cognitive Functions Test: the Eight Function-Attitudes
seoDescription: What Jung’s eight function-attitudes are — thinking, feeling, sensation, and intuition, each introverted or extraverted — and how a free quiz can score them.
title: Jung’s eight function-attitudes
lede: Jung did not measure a four-letter code. He described four functions, each able to turn toward the outer object or toward the inner impression a thing leaves, and that gives eight function-attitudes, which is what this quiz is built to score.

sections.heading: What a function-attitude is
paragraphs: In Psychological Types, a function is a way the psyche orients: thinking judges by a concept, feeling judges by value, sensation takes the given fact, and intuition takes what the fact could become or already implies. Extraversion and introversion are not sociability. They say where that function points — toward the object in the shared world, or toward the subjective factor, the impression, image, or standard the object leaves in the person.

That pairing is the function-attitude. Introverted intuition is not “quiet intuition,” and extraverted feeling is not “being nice.” Each of the eight has a different object and a different test of what counts as real, which is why a quiz that only asks whether you like parties cannot tell them apart.

sections.heading: The eight, in brief
paragraphs: Introverted intuition (Ni) waits on an inner picture of where a situation is tending. Extraverted intuition (Ne) scents what an outer situation could become and keeps several paths in play. Introverted sensation (Si) compares the present with the impression already stored in body and memory. Extraverted sensation (Se) takes the concrete scene as it is given — texture, timing, impact.

Introverted thinking (Ti) wants the idea itself to be consistent, even before it is useful. Extraverted thinking (Te) wants a conclusion others can check and a result that can be arranged. Introverted feeling (Fi) measures a choice against a private standard of worth. Extraverted feeling (Fe) reads the feeling-tone among the people involved and asks whether the we can still hold.

sections.heading: Why close pairs are hard
paragraphs: The pairs that confuse people are usually the same function in two attitudes, or two judging functions that both feel like “being right.” Ni and Ne can both look visionary. Fi and Ti can both look stubborn. Si and Se can both look practical. Fe and Te can both look like they are running the room. A single adjective will not separate them. You have to ask where the function points, and what it treats as a finished reason.

This quiz uses forty-eight statements, six for each function-attitude, including a reverse-keyed item, and if two leads land together it asks a short follow-up of forced choices rather than another set of ratings. The free result is the eight scores and a likely type. The longer Beebe reading sits in Your Type in Depth.

sections.heading: What the scores are not
paragraphs: A high bar is a preference on these items, not a talent certificate and not a medical finding. Jung wrote about living processes, which can move, fatigue, and fall into the unconscious. Beebe’s later eight-role model is one way of reading how those processes sit in a type; it is a map, not a sentence passed upon you.
If you want the functions in your own words before you rate the statements, the close-pair guides are the next place to read, and then the quiz.

seoTitle: Jungian Functions vs MBTI®: What This Quiz Measures
seoDescription: How a Jungian cognitive functions quiz differs from the Myers-Briggs Type Indicator: eight function-attitudes first, then a type as a reading aid, not an official MBTI result.
title: Jungian functions and MBTI®
lede: People search for an MBTI test and land on function language, or the other way around, and the words get used as if they were the same instrument. They are not, and this page is here so you can see what you are taking before you begin.

sections.heading: What Jung wrote
paragraphs: Jung’s Psychological Types (1921) describes four functions and two attitudes. The type, when he names one, is a sketch of which function leads and whether it is turned inward or outward. He did not publish a multiple-choice inventory, and he did not treat the remaining functions as a simple list of letters to collect.

A Jungian functions quiz, if it is honest, therefore starts with the eight function-attitudes and only afterwards asks which classical stack those scores resemble. The letters, if they appear, are a shorthand for that stack, not the thing that was measured.

sections.heading: What MBTI® is
paragraphs: The Myers-Briggs Type Indicator is a separate, trademarked instrument. It sorts preferences along four dichotomies and reports a four-letter type. It has its own items, its own manuals, and its own publisher. It is not this site, and this site is not affiliated with it.

Many popular “MBTI tests” on the internet are unofficial quizzes that borrow the letters. Some of them never score the functions at all. Others guess a function stack from the letters after the fact. That last step can be useful as a reading, but it is not the same as asking you about Ni, Te, Fi, and Se as Jung described them.

sections.heading: What this quiz does
paragraphs: You rate forty-eight original statements about how each function-attitude works in you. The first stretch looks for the leading function. If two functions are still close, a follow-up asks which sentence is more you. The result is eight 0–100% bars and a suggested type whose Beebe stack fits those bars, with the lead weighted first.

The quiz, the scores, and the choice of Hero / Heroine and Parent stay free. Your Type in Depth is a longer reading of the eight roles, growth, and shadow. Compatibility is a second, separate unlock. Neither is an MBTI report.

sections.heading: When to use which
paragraphs: If you need the official MBTI instrument for work or certification, take it from a licensed provider. If you want an educational reading of Jung’s eight function-attitudes, scored in the browser with no account, this quiz is built for that, and the letters it shows are a way of naming the stack, not a claim to be Myers-Briggs.

seoTitle: Ni vs Ne: Introverted and Extraverted Intuition
seoDescription: The difference between introverted intuition (Ni) and extraverted intuition (Ne): one inner trajectory vs a field of outer possibilities, and how a quiz can tell them apart.
title: Ni vs Ne
lede: Both attitudes of intuition look ahead of the given facts, which is why they are so often confused, and the difference is not how imaginative you are but where the possibility is seen — as one inner picture, or as a field of outer forks that are not yet real.

sections.heading: Where each one looks
paragraphs: Introverted intuition is oriented by the inner object. A direction arrives as if you had already seen the end of the story, often before you can show the steps, and further options can feel like noise once that picture has settled. Extraverted intuition is oriented by the object-world. One outer fact suggests several paths that are not yet real, and interest often moves on once a possibility has been realized.

Ni withdraws from the room to consult an image. Ne stays with the room and scents the next connection in the objects and people themselves. Both can be quiet. Both can talk too much. The test is not volume. It is whether the unused door is inside, or still on the table.

sections.heading: How they show in a day
paragraphs: A day led by Ni often begins with a problem rearranging itself before the kettle has boiled, and it goes poorly when you live only in the destination and then call the world late for not having arrived. A day led by Ne branches, and it goes poorly when every door is kept open so that Tuesday never has to be named.

People who lead with the other attitude can look like a threat to the one you trust. Ne can feel to Ni like sabotage, a hail of alternatives against a vision that had just become whole. Ni can feel to Ne like a premature close, one fate declared against a field that was still alive.

sections.heading: What the quiz asks
paragraphs: The Ni items ask whether inner images show the direction before the outer facts are complete, and whether you would rather follow one unfolding vision than keep many outer options in play. The Ne items ask whether you notice what a situation could become, and whether you feel most alive when the field of outer options is still open. Each bank has a reverse item written in the other attitude, so that a person who only likes “being intuitive” does not inflate both bars.

If Ni and Ne still land together after the first stretch, the follow-up is five forced choices, not another Likert scale. You pick the sentence that is more you, and those votes are folded into the percentages so that one of them can lead.

sections.heading: Take the items next
paragraphs: If you have been typed as an intuitive and still cannot tell whether the future arrives as one trajectory or as a field of forks, the forty-eight statements are built to ask that, and the result will show both scores even if only one of them leads.

seoTitle: Fi vs Ti: Introverted Feeling and Introverted Thinking
seoDescription: The difference between introverted feeling (Fi) and introverted thinking (Ti): a private standard of worth vs an inner model that has to be consistent, and how to tell them apart.
title: Fi vs Ti
lede: Both introverted judging functions can look like stubbornness from the outside, because neither will trade its inner standard for a popular formula, and the difference is what the court is deciding — whether this is right for me, or whether the idea holds.

sections.heading: What each court is for
paragraphs: Introverted feeling orients by a private standard of worth. A choice can be wrong even when it is popular, and the intensity of that verdict often shows very little. You may know what you love or reject before you can justify it in public terms, and collective taste does not settle the question.

Introverted thinking orients by the consistency of the idea. A popular explanation bothers you if it is logically hollow, and you would rather refine a definition than apply a ready-made formula. You think in order to understand, not first of all in order to arrange the outer world, and a plan that merely works can still feel unfinished if you cannot say why.

sections.heading: Why they score close
paragraphs: A person who hates being pushed can endorse both a value item and a logic item, because both are ways of refusing the group. The quiz therefore includes reverse-keyed statements: Fi’s reverse is taking on the values the people around you hold, and Ti’s reverse is being satisfied if a plan works even when you cannot explain it. Those items exist so that “I am independent” does not raise every introverted bar at once.

When Fi and Ti both land high, the first forty-eight ratings are often not enough, which is common and not a failure of the test. The follow-up asks which finished the decision — a private yes or no you may not be able to display, or a definition that has to hold together — and which you keep if you cannot satisfy both: what you consider right, or what you consider true.

sections.heading: In relation to other people
paragraphs: Fi can feel to others like being deeply chosen, or like being dropped for failing a test they were never shown. Ti can feel like respect for the idea, or like being dissected. Neither is extraverted feeling, which would ask whether the room can still stand together, and neither is extraverted thinking, which would ask whether the result can be shown.

If your old four-letter type left you between INFP and INTP, or between ISFP and ISTP, this pair is usually the hinge, and the scores will not be honest until the follow-up has been answered in your own words rather than in the words of a profile you already liked.

sections.heading: Take the items next
paragraphs: The quiz does not ask you to pick a letter. It asks whether a clever argument still feels unfinished if it injures what you value, or whether a sincere feeling still feels unfinished if the idea does not hold, and that is a better question than which aesthetic you prefer.

seoTitle: INFP vs INFJ: Same Letters, Different Stacks
seoDescription: INFP and INFJ share three letters and no cognitive functions. Why the J/P code misleads, how Fi-Ne differs from Ni-Fe, and how a functions quiz tells them apart.
title: INFP vs INFJ
lede: Their four letter code looks alike, which is perhaps why so many people bounce between them…but they are not close types.

paragraphs: INFJ and INFP share no function-attitudes. The last letter makes a big difference. It is the difference between a psyche led by introverted intuition and a psyche led by introverted feeling.
**INFJ : Introverted Intuition (Ni), Extraverted Feeling (Fe), Introverted Thinking (Ti), and Extraverted Sensing (Se).**
**INFP : Introverted Feeling (Fi), Extroverted Intuition (Ne), Introverted Sensing (Si) , and Extroverted Thinking (Te).**

sections.heading: The last letter is a lie
paragraphs: For an introvert, the J/P letter describes the attitude of the **extraverted** function, not the dominant one. That is why an INFJ is technically a **J type**, while its dominant function, introverted intuition (Ni), is actually a perceiving function.

**INFJ is therefore a dominant perceiving type.** Ni tends to form an inner picture of where things are heading before arriving at a definite conclusion. An INFJ may sense the pattern, direction, or meaning of something before they can fully explain what they think about it.

**INFP, by contrast, is a dominant judging type.** Its dominant function, introverted feeling (Fi), evaluates experience according to an internal sense of value and authenticity. The INFP may know internally that something feels right or wrong before they have fully worked out the surrounding situation.
**INFJ:** Ni–Fe–Ti–Se → **dominant Ni (perceiving)**
**INFP:** Fi–Ne–Si–Te → **dominant Fi (judging)**

sections.heading: Two stacks, eight roles
paragraphs: In Beebe’s model, the eight cognitive functions are understood as eight different roles within the personality. The most important distinction between INFJ and INFP is where the **Hero / Heroine** sits.

For **INFJ**, the Hero / Heroine is **introverted intuition (Ni)**. Ni is concerned with the inner pattern: where things are going, what they mean, and what they may eventually become. It tends to form a picture of the underlying trajectory before everything can be explained or acted upon.

The **Parent** is **extraverted feeling (Fe)**. Fe brings that inner perception into the shared world. It notices the emotional atmosphere, considers the needs of others, and tries to create a human context in which the vision can be understood or lived.
The **Eternal Child** is **introverted thinking (Ti)**: the private search for precision, consistency, and the underlying reason something is true.

The **Inferior** is **extraverted sensation (Se)**: direct contact with the immediate, physical world. This is the present moment, the concrete fact, the body, and the thing that is actually happening now. For an Ni-dominant person, this immediate reality can feel intrusive when the inner picture has not yet been completed.
For **INFP**, the arrangement is different.
The Hero / Heroine is **introverted feeling (Fi)**. Fi is the private compass of value: what feels true, meaningful, authentic, or morally right to the individual.

The **Parent** is **extraverted intuition (Ne)**. Ne opens possibilities around that inner compass. It asks what else could be possible, what another interpretation might be, or which unexplored path might allow the person's values to be expressed.
The **Eternal Child** is **introverted sensation (Si)**: familiarity, memory, continuity, and the known world that provides a sense of inner stability.
The **Inferior** is **extraverted thinking (Te)**: external structure, measurable results, efficiency, decisions, and the demand to make something objectively work.
This produces an important difference.
**INFJ leads with a perception of where things are going. INFP leads with a judgment about what is true to the self.**

That is why an INFJ can appear quite decisive from the outside while internally still be living inside an unfinished picture. And it is why an INFP can appear open-ended or indecisive while internally holding a remarkably firm sense of what they can and cannot accept.
The difference is not simply *planned versus spontaneous*. It is **perception first versus evaluation first**.

sections.heading: Intensity, and the quieter court
paragraphs: Both types can care intensely about meaning. Both can be private. Both can be sensitive to people and experiences. The important question is what happens **first**.

INFJ tends toward a search for the underlying trajectory: *Where is this going? What does this mean? What is really happening beneath the surface?* Once that perception forms, Fe often turns toward the human world and asks how it can be communicated, shared, or made meaningful among people.

This can make the INFJ appear socially certain even when the inner perception is still developing. Fe can read a room quickly and respond to it naturally, but that social responsiveness should not be mistaken for the source of the personality's deepest orientation. The Hero remains Ni: the inner picture comes first.

INFP tends toward a quieter kind of fidelity. Fi continually evaluates experience against an internal sense of value: *Is this true for me? Does this violate something I believe? Does this feel authentic?*

New people and new experiences may therefore be approached cautiously. Reserve does not necessarily mean rejection. The person may simply be waiting to discover how the experience sits with their inner values.

This is why kindness itself is not a reliable way to distinguish the two. An INFJ may be highly attuned to the emotional climate through Fe, while an INFP may be deeply compassionate through Fi. They can look similar from the outside.
The better question is:
**Is the first movement toward a perception of what is happening and where it is going, or toward an inner judgment about what is true and valuable?**

sections.heading: What can be thought, and what cannot
paragraphs: INFJ's **Ti** occupies the Eternal Child position. This gives the INFJ an ability to become absorbed in analysis for its own sake. An idea can be followed simply because it is interesting, even when the conclusion is uncomfortable.

This can produce a willingness to question moral, psychological, or philosophical assumptions that initially seemed obvious. A carefully constructed system of beliefs can suddenly be taken apart because one distinction has exposed a contradiction.

That is both a strength and a potential source of disruption. The INFJ's Fe can make them appear warm, understanding, and morally oriented, while the Ti underneath may be quietly asking whether the entire framework actually makes sense.

INFP's **Ne**, by contrast, serves Fi. Possibilities are explored in relation to the inner value system. Ne can generate an enormous number of interpretations and alternatives, but those possibilities are ultimately being brought back to the question of meaning and personal truth.

This is why an INFP may enjoy exploring possibilities without wanting to dismantle its deepest values simply for the pleasure of analysis. Possibility is useful when it reveals another way for something meaningful to exist.
Neither approach is more intelligent.
The difference is in **what the exploration is serving**.
INFJ's Ti can ask: *Is this actually true? Does the whole structure hold together?*
INFP's Fi can ask: *Is this actually meaningful? Is this faithful to what matters?*

Each can therefore misunderstand the other. The INFJ may see the INFP as unwilling to question its deepest assumptions. The INFP may see the INFJ as willing to sacrifice meaning for the sake of intellectual consistency.

sections.heading: The act, and the visitation
paragraphs: The INFJ often carries an inner picture of something that should eventually exist in the shared world: a work, a truth, a relationship, a way of living, or some larger realization that needs to become tangible.

But **Se**, as the inferior function, can make direct engagement with the immediate world strangely difficult. The vision may be vivid while the practical execution feels clumsy, distracting, or disappointingly ordinary.

Fe often helps bridge that gap. It brings the inner vision into relationship with other people and gives it a social form. But the INFJ can still feel that the concrete world has not quite caught up with what they perceive internally.
The INFP's movement is different.

Fi first establishes what matters. Ne then looks outward for possibilities through which that inner value might be expressed. Rather than imposing a single trajectory, it can wait for an unexpected opening: *What else could this become? Where is the possibility I have not considered yet?*
This can give the INFP an almost **visitation-like** relationship with possibility. Inspiration may arrive through a person, an idea, an artwork, a place, or an unexpected connection.

The inferior **Te** creates the opposite problem. When external demands become unavoidable, the INFP may suddenly feel pressured to organize, quantify, decide, produce, or prove. Te can appear as a last-minute tyrant: *Just make a decision. Finish it. Make it measurable.*
But once a workable external structure is discovered, the INFP can become surprisingly steady. The outer structure is valuable because it protects something internal.
For the INFP, the question is often:
**How can the outer world be arranged so that the inner life can remain intact?**
For the INFJ, the question is more often:
**How can the inner picture become real in the outer world?**
That difference is subtle, but fundamental.

sections.heading: Take the items next
paragraphs: Under stress, either type can temporarily resemble another type.

An INFJ can retreat into **Ti**, becoming unusually analytical, detached, or preoccupied with solving a problem intellectually. An INFP can fall into **Te**, becoming unusually rigid, controlling, efficiency-focused, or concerned with measurable results.
These states do not mean the person's type has changed. They are expressions of less-developed functions under pressure.

This is also why a four-letter test taken during a difficult period can produce confusing results. Someone who normally leads with Ni may answer questions in a way that makes them look like an analytical type. Someone who normally leads with Fi may answer in a way that makes them look highly structured or decisive.
So if you have repeatedly come out as both **INFJ and INFP**, don't begin with questions like:
*Am I organised or messy?*
*Do I like plans or spontaneity?*
*Am I decisive or flexible?*
Those behaviours can be produced by many different things.
Instead, look at the **first mental movement**.
Does your mind naturally begin by forming an inner picture of **where something is going and what it means**?
That points toward **introverted intuition (Ni)** and INFJ.
Or does it naturally begin by determining **what is true, valuable, authentic, or right for you**?
That points toward **introverted feeling (Fi)** and INFP.
The difference is not between a person who plans and a person who does not.
It is between **a mind that first perceives a pattern** and **a mind that first evaluates according to an inner value**.
Take the items next. Rather than asking you to choose a four-letter label, they will ask you to recognise which of these underlying movements is more consistently your own.

seoTitle: Si vs Se: Introverted and Extraverted Sensation
seoDescription: The difference between introverted sensation (Si) and extraverted sensation (Se): stored impression and precedent vs the concrete scene as it is now.
title: Si vs Se
lede: Both attitudes of sensation stay with the actual, which is why they can both look “practical,” and the difference is whether the present is complete in itself or incomplete until it has been compared with the impression already lived in the body.

sections.heading: What each one takes as real
paragraphs: Introverted sensation notices first the impression an object leaves, not only its public properties. The present is vivid when it echoes something already lived, and a new situation is judged by that inner store of sensory memory. A thing can look ordinary to others and still carry a dense private texture.

Extraverted sensation trusts the concrete facts of this moment more than a theory about them. Texture, movement, timing, and impact say what is real, and attention locks onto the actual object or scene. Pleasure, pain, and aesthetic impact in the present guide the next move, and a hidden meaning can wait.

sections.heading: How they part in a new scene
paragraphs: When a new scene opens, Si asks whether this matches how such things have felt and gone. Se asks what can be seen, touched, and done now, even if there is no precedent. Si returns to what has already proved itself. Se returns to what is actually happening.

That is why a high Si score is not “being old-fashioned,” and a high Se score is not “being impulsive,” though those cartoons exist. Si can be exact about a craft. Se can be exact about a room. The cartoon begins when you use one word, sensing, for both.

sections.heading: What the quiz asks
paragraphs: The Si items ask whether familiar sequences and bodily baselines tell you whether something is as it should be, and the reverse item asks whether you take the sensory world as it appears now without referring it to past impressions. The Se items ask whether you would rather act on what is here than wait for a hidden meaning, and the reverse item asks whether the present scene feels less real than the inner impression it leaves.

If the two bars stay close, the follow-up asks what you notice first, how you judge whether a situation can be trusted, and which sentence is nearer: that the present is incomplete until the inner sensory texture has been consulted, or that the present is enough.

sections.heading: Take the items next
paragraphs: If you have been told you are “a sensing type” and still cannot tell whether you live in the archive or in the scene, rate the statements as they are written, not as a defense of a letter you already wear.

seoTitle: Fe vs Te: Extraverted Feeling and Extraverted Thinking
seoDescription: The difference between extraverted feeling (Fe) and extraverted thinking (Te): keeping the feeling-tone of the group vs arranging a result others can check.
title: Fe vs Te
stat: two ways of running the shared world
lede: Both extraverted judging functions organize what is between people, which is why they can both look like leadership, and the difference is what counts as a finished plan — that the we can still stand together, or that the work produced what it said it would.

sections.heading: What each one organizes
paragraphs: Extraverted feeling knows what is fitting by reading the feeling-tone of the people involved. It adjusts what is shown so that the relation stays intact, and the received value of the group — what “one” does — weighs on the choice. A decision that is logically neat can still feel unfinished if it injures the group.

Extraverted thinking trusts a conclusion more when it follows from data others can also check. It organizes people, time, and facts according to an objective standard, and an argument that cannot be put to a practical test soon loses it. Results that can be shown matter more than the elegance of an inner theory.

sections.heading: When a group effort is failing
paragraphs: Fe notices first that morale and the feeling-tone have broken, even if the metrics still look tidy. Te notices first that the procedure is not producing, even if everyone still feels loyal to it. If you cannot satisfy both, Fe keeps harmony and Te keeps effectiveness, and each will call the other unfinished.

Neither is introverted feeling, which would keep a private standard even if the room disagrees, and neither is introverted thinking, which would keep the inner model even if it is not yet useful. The extraverted pair is about the shared world. That is why they so often compete for the same jobs, committees, and family roles.

sections.heading: What the quiz asks
paragraphs: The Fe items ask whether you feel responsible for whether the atmosphere between people is bearable, and the reverse item says the group’s mood does not change what you consider right. The Te items ask whether you want thinking to produce an order that works in the shared world, and the reverse item would rather keep an inner theory coherent than make it work outside.

When Fe and Te are close, the follow-up asks what made a plan finished, what you actually organize — the atmosphere, or the shared measures — and which test you use: whether you can still stand together, or whether this worked in facts others can check.

sections.heading: Take the items next
paragraphs: If you have been called a leader and still cannot tell whether you are keeping the climate or the output, the statements are written to force that choice, and the eight scores will show the other six functions as well, so that the lead is not the only story.
